public_payload.normalized_proposition: If his thesis is right, OpenAI's death will kill most or all other AI startups, including Anthropic, and every AI investor will take massive losses.

statement.excerpt: And if I’m right, OpenAI’s death will kill off most if not all other AI startups, Anthropic included. Every investor that invested in AI will take massive losses.

from_speaker: kill off most if not all other AI startups
Every investor that invested in AI
our_interpretation: The operative antecedent is OpenAI's business failure and cessation of its core services. A financing difficulty, model retirement or temporary outage does not meet it.
I treat if I'm right as introducing the collapse scenario, not as making the forecast true by definition.
Most means more than half of the other AI startups operating immediately before that collapse. Anthropic must also fail.
Every investor is a universal claim about investors with AI exposure before the collapse. Massive means a substantial loss of invested capital, but the speaker supplies no numerical threshold.
The forecast requires evidence that OpenAI's failure caused the other failures and losses; unrelated closures do not suffice.
criteria.support_condition: After a documented OpenAI collapse, more than half of the defined startup population, including Anthropic, fail because of it, and every investor in the defined population suffers substantial AI-investment losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After the antecedent, decisive final records establish that a required consequence cannot occur, such as an investor completing all relevant exits without substantial losses. Mere continued startup survival for an evaluator-selected interval is insufficient.
